newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica seen gaining on int'l alliance. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Telefonica seen gaining on int'l alliance. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]

text.p: Telefonica shares are seen likely to gain after news on Friday that it has reached a global alliance with British Telecommunications and U.S. group MCI Communications Corp, dealers said.

But they were unsure how much further headway the stock could immediately make after soaring near four percent in the last week, and views were mixed on whether the alliance news had already been discounted.
At 1015 GMT, Telefonica was down 5 pesetas, 0.14 percent, to 3,560, outperforming the Ibex-35 blue chip index which was down 0.58 percent to 5,596.43.
"There's no doubt it's very good news, and it may not be in the price. I'd expect it to close slightly positively today, maybe adding around 10 pesetas," said a foreign brokerage dealer.

Most of the day's heavy volume -- already nearing three million shares at midday-- was due to trading, rather than final investors. Typically, Telefonica trades some three to five million shares a day.

The deal involves BT buying two percent of Telefonica over the next twelve months, and this coupled with the purchase of a one percent stake by Portugal Telecom augured well for the share price on a broader time horizon.

"Taking into account those purchases, which make up around four (corrects from 40) million shares, the stock simply has to climb. We've got an 18-month target price of 3,900 and its a long way off," the dealer added.
A trader at a Spanish brokerage expected the shares to consolidate before climbing further.

"I think the news of the alliance has been discounted. You only have to look at what the shares have done in the past week. I think we'll see it pause for breath before making further headway," she said.
